ENGLISH MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ENGLISH MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

3. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.

5. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.

8. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. goed

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Phrases: adverb adjective and prepositional phrases and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 5.4.1 Functional Writing ● inventory ● condolence notes ● headline langu and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking ● Responsive Listening: Interpretive listening and making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Sounds and stress ● sounds: double consonant cluste and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
